notes: Scope: reworked packages/world/src/noise/** (perlin.ts, fbm.ts, climate.ts, index.ts) and added packages/world/src/__tests__/world-b.noise.test.ts (28 tests). Exported names, argument order and the NoiseBasis / WarpResult / CreateNoiseBasis shapes from src/internal.ts are unchanged, so src/index.ts, src/terrain/**, src/biome/** and src/features/** keep compiling untouched.

Output is bit-identical to L1-A's v1 for every field. Verified two ways: ~40 pinned values in the new test (perlin2, perlin3, fbm2, fbm3, ridged2, warp2, climateAt, seeds 1337 and 20260916) and an accumulated-sum probe over 5 chunks comparing v1 extracted from 395745d against the working tree (job 36a8525b2ffa4082).
golden.json is untouched. pnpm --filter @voxelcraft/world run golden:update was NOT run and no golden hash changed, because the improvements are structural and value-preserving.

Performance: noise work per chunk went from 1.0981 ms (v1) to 0.9075 ms, a 1.21x speedup saving about 0.19 ms per chunk. For context, world-a's perf test reports full chunkGen averaging 6.471 ms against PERF.chunkGenBudgetMs 4 and BENCH.chunkGenAvgMsMax 6; the remaining gap is outside the noise layer (column fill and features) and belongs to L1-A / world-c.

Regression found and fixed inside this task. The first v2 pass (4234e19) hand-inlined the lattice dot products and the interpolation tree and switched the gradient tables to Int8Array. A variant benchmark (job 4c28dd12bc9543ad) showed that made noise 16-19% SLOWER than v1: the sampler bodies grow past what V8 will inline into the fBm octave loops, and plain array + inlined was worst at 1.37x v1. c6dc219 restores the small monomorphic dot2/dot3/lerp helpers and the plain gradient tables. The measured numbers are recorded in a comment at the top of perlin.ts so the inlining is not reintroduced.

Kept from the v2 pass: the *Raw split, so the finite-input check runs once per field sample instead of once per octave; Float64Array scratch buffers in warp2To / warpStages2 / climateAt, which remove roughly 512 short-lived WarpResult objects per chunk; and non-finite guards that return 0 at the public entry points instead of letting NaN reach terrain.

Determinism: gradients come only from hashU32, so a sample never depends on call order, instance identity or worker. No unseeded entropy, no wall clock and no trigonometry anywhere in generation code. Note for future editors: world-a.terrain.test.ts scans source text, so those forbidden token strings must not appear under packages/world/src even inside comments; one red run was caused by a doc comment mentioning them.

One assertion is deliberately loose: the createNoiseBasis instance-identity test requires more than 190 of 240 off-lattice samples to differ between seeds instead of all 240. With an 8-entry 2D gradient table two seeds can legitimately select the same gradient pair, so a handful of exact ties is expected. Determinism itself is still asserted exactly, with 0 mismatches.

Ownership respected: packages/core-types, docs/orchestration, root config, CI and all dependency declarations are untouched, no dependency was added or bumped, and the src/internal.ts constants (NOISE_FIELDS, TERRAIN, BIOME_RULES, CAVES) were left to L1-A. No contract change is needed.
